    The Krull–Schmidt theorem for modules of finite length #

    • Existence: an Artinian module is isomorphic to a finite product Π i, X i of indecomposable modules (exists_linearEquiv_pi).
    • Exchange: if an indecomposable module P with local endomorphism ring is a direct summand of Π j, X j with every X j indecomposable, then P ≅ X j for some j (exists_nonempty_linearEquiv_of_comp_eq_id). This is the cancellation form used in the proof of Theorem 5.2.
    • Uniqueness: two decompositions of a module of finite length into finitely many indecomposables agree up to a bijection of the index sets and isomorphisms of the summands (krullSchmidt).

    Each statement has a ModuleCat form with biproducts ⨁ X and a form with finite dimension stated through RestrictScalars k A, as in Statement.dim. Finite products are used instead of direct sums since the index sets are finite.

    The existence part follows the module specialization in Modules/KrullSchmidt/FiniteModuleDecomposition.lean of multiplicative-bases-deformations at commit 7b9f39f221d8a420a1531f487a3b93ae6d26ce85, with induction on submodules instead of dimension. The uniqueness part is the standard exchange argument.
